articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Named Giants QB1 Over Jameis Winston for Giants' NFL Week 7 Game vs. Texans
articles.summary: The New York Giants have a new starter under center.
articles.body:
The New York Giants have a new starter under center.

J.J. McCarthy will take over for Jameis Winston in Week 7 against the Houston Texans, head coach John Harbaugh announced on Wednseaday.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler initially reported the Giants planned to start McCarthy at quarterback over Winston.

New York initially acquired McCarthy in a trade with the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 28, sending out a 2027 fifth-round draft pick in exchange for the signal-caller.

He served as a depth piece for the Giants before entering their first-team offense after Winston was benched in the second half of a 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints in Week 6.

McCarthy didn't get off to a hot start against New Orleans, as he threw an interception on his first drive of the game.

Still, he bounced back and nearly helped the Giants pull off an improbable comeback victory. They trailed 34-10 at the time McCarthy entered the game in the fourth quarter before cutting the deficit to 34-27.

New York also had an opportunity to tie the game on its final possession, but couldn't convert on fourth down at the Saints' 14-yard line.

McCarthy finished 11-of-21 for 243 yards and one touchdown while getting picked off once, as Winston went 14-of-26 for 152 yards and one touchdown compared to a pair of interceptions.

McCarthy is looking to get is career back on track, as the former first-round pick failed to meet expectations as a member of the Vikings.

In 2024, he was sidelined for his entire rookie season due to a torn meniscus .

McCarthy struggled the following year, completing 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards and 11 touchdowns to go along with 12 interceptions in 10 games. He was also unable to beat out Kyler Murray in a training camp battle for Minnesota's first-string quarterback job heading into his 2026 campaign.

As for Winston, he's started in each of the Giants' four games since Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2.

Winston has thrown for 957 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions while posting a 57.0 completion percentage.

The Giants have still opened their 2026 season on a high note despite utilizing multiple starting quarterbacks, sitting atop the NFC East standings with a 3-2-1 record.

They'll face the Texans on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Titans coach Robert Saleh offers support for Jordan Elliott after gun incident: 'A terrible lapse in judgement'
articles.summary: Jordan Elliott still has support from Titans coach Robert Saleh.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh made it clear he still supports Jordan Elliott following the defensive tackle's release due to reportedly having a gun at a team facility . Saleh spoke about the situation Wednesday, giving an impassioned speech in Elliott's defense while also using the moment to speak on mental-health awareness in the sport.

Elliott was released by the team Tuesday. At the time, the Titans cited " an incident at our team facility ," but did not go into detail on what led to Elliott's release. Early Wednesday, a report emerged suggesting Elliott went to retrieve a gun from his car after a practice dispute with another player. The NFL prohibits players from having firearms at a team or league facility.

Saleh confirmed aspects of those reports Wednesday, saying Elliott "pulled a gun in the parking lot." Instead of admonishing Elliott for his actions, Saleh chose to focus on mental health, asking what would cause a player like Elliott to resort to such drastic measures.

Saleh opened his comments crediting the Titans and the NFL for the way both sides handled the situation. He immediately showed support for Elliott, calling him "a father, a great husband" and someone who has "never committed a crime in his entire life."

Saleh then confirmed Elliott "pulled a gun in the parking lot." He then asked what would cause a player like Elliott — who Saleh said was a hard worker and well-liked in the locker room — to "go off the rails and grab a gun."

The coach then referred to it as a "cry for help." He said the team and NFL checked every single box "with regards to getting [Elliott] the help that he needs."

Saleh then referenced two NFL players who took their own lives due to mental-health issues. While Saleh did not mention those players by name, he may have been referring to Dallas Cowboys defensive end Marshawn Kneeland and Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Rondale Moore, both of whom died by suicide in the past year.

Saleh said he wasn't going to speak on whether Elliott was dealing with something similar, but used the moment to convey how much physical and mental stress NFL players are under.

Saleh then took a moment to go to bat for Elliott's character. The coach said he understood the NFL rules, seemingly agreeing with the team's decision to release Elliott, but added he would speak highly of Elliott to any other team that wanted to pick up the defensive tackle.

"I will stand on the table for Jordan's character," Saleh said. "Unfortunately, rules are rules with regards to guns on property and sometimes it's far greater than the knee-jerk reaction of kicking somebody when they are down. "My message to 31 other teams would be if you need a hell of a run-stopping D-tackle that can help you on a playoff run, give me a call and I'll tell you everything you need to know about him. "He's a good man. Had a terrible lapse in judgement that I recognize as a call for help more than a critical act. And it's unfortunate the way it went down. But as far as Jordan is concerned and the locker room and all that … I think people see it differently here than the knee-jerk reaction of the world."

But as far as Jordan is concerned and the locker room and all that … I think people see it differently here than the knee-jerk reaction of the world."

Saleh wasn't the only member of the organization to speak out in support of Elliott. All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons called Elliott an "unbelievable teammate."

Simmons then spoke out in support of mental health and making sure players speak to a professional when in need of help.

Toward the end of his statement, Simmons expressed a desire to move forward as an organization and turned the focus to the team's Week 7 game against the Cleveland Browns.

articles.title: Sam LaPorta expresses disappointment Lions haven't extended him yet; TE prepared to 'get paid somewhere else'
articles.summary: LaPorta remains committed to playing for Detroit, but he conveyed on Barstool's "Pardon My Take" that he's dismayed the franchise hasn't given him a new deal...
articles.body:
Four years ago, the Detroit Lions traded tight end T.J. Hockenson to the Minnesota Vikings midseason. The Vikings wound up signing him to a then-record-setting extension in the summer of 2023.

Hockenson's eventual replacement in Detroit, Sam LaPorta, is now due for a lucrative extension.

He's in the final year of his rookie deal, and, despite his impressive play upon returning from a back injury that cut his 2025 campaign short , the Lions still haven't extended him.

LaPorta, an Iowa product like Hockenson, expressed his disappointment in that situation during the latest episode of Barstool's "Pardon My Take" podcast.

The 2023 second-round pick was asked about playing with the uncertainty of his NFL future looming.

"I think the combination of getting your heartstrings twisted as well as the violent sport that we play, it sucks," LaPorta said. "And it's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt. Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f***ing back for the team. And then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love. "So it sucks. I'm going to continue to be a pro, and I dish a lot of that to my agent, and he handles that great. ... So I'm going to continue to go do my thing and ball out. And in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good. I'll go get paid somewhere else."

"And it's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt. Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f***ing back for the team. And then I'm going out there this year, and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love.

"So it sucks. I'm going to continue to be a pro, and I dish a lot of that to my agent, and he handles that great. ... So I'm going to continue to go do my thing and ball out. And in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good. I'll go get paid somewhere else."

LaPorta has been "balling." In five games this season, he's already piled up 27 catches, 316 receiving yards and 3 touchdown grabs.

The 25-year-old currently ranks fifth among all tight ends in receiving yards this season, and he's coming off a bye week.

LaPorta, who made the Pro Bowl and earned second-team All-Pro honors as a rookie in 2023, said on Tuesday's episode of "Pardon My Take" that he had a microdiscectomy last November. That procedure was necessary to address his herniated disc.

"So we're coming up on like 11 months, almost a year, but feeling good," LaPorta said. "I was talking to someone this morning actually about it, and I made the example: In training camp, we go live a little bit, but your teammates are still going to take it easy on you. So Week 1, you know, you take a couple of shots, and you kind of bounce up off the turf like, 'Oh yeah, I guess I can still do this. I can get smoked, get up and go back in and play like 90% of the snaps or whatever it was.' "So it's just kind of an eye-opening moment, but cool to bounce back from that."

So far this season, he's logged at least 56 offensive snaps in all five of the games the 3-2 Lions have played, according to Pro Football Focus.

He's once again been a reliable target for quarterback Jared Goff and a willing blocker for a Detroit offense that loves to run the ball, too.

articles.title: Jerry Jones Addresses Stance on Coaching Changes amid Schottenheimer Buzz with Cowboys at 2-4
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones offered more insight into the decision to bring aboard Mike Pettine to serve as a senior assistant to defensive coordinator Christian Parker while speaking to reporters on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones offered more insight into the decision to bring aboard Mike Pettine to serve as a senior assistant to defensive coordinator Christian Parker while speaking to reporters on Wednesday.

"[Pettine] had a background with our coordinators and was with us in the spring," he noted. "It fit. He wanted to come help. That's a pretty significant qualifier for somebody that has that kind of background with everybody involved. So, it was as much about his uniqueness as it was about what we wanted to do to help us play better."

On Monday, executive vice president Stephen Jones made it clear that head coach Brian Schottenheimer—who has a 9-13-1 record in his second season as head coach—still has the full support of ownership.

"Absolutely. There's not any question in Jerry's and I's mind," he said during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. "He has the team. There's no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen. We feel really good... about our coaching staff. We just have to continue to evolve and get to a point where we can win these football games."

The Cowboys are just 2-4 to start the 2026 season, in large part due to a defense that ranks 25th in points allowed (26.5 PPG) and 30th in yards allowed (382.5 YPG). As the Cowboys continue to adjust to first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker and his scheme, more additions could be coming to that side of the ball.

"I'll be real clear: I would be active if we could get a chance to help the team this year," Jones told reporters. "That's important."

Given that the NFC East is wide open this season—only the New York Giants (3-2-1) have a winning record in the division—Dallas' slow start hasn't buried its playoff aspirations just yet.

"It gives me a lot of promise," Jones said. "I see opportunity. And I see it legitimately because I know the things that we have the potential to do, both with our talent, both our schemes, adjustments I've seen us do in the spring—the kinds of adjustments that you might want to do between the halves."

The Cowboys still have four more games against divisional opponents, including Sunday's matchup against the injury-ravaged Philadelphia Eagles. It may be too early to declare it a must-win contest for Dallas, but losing against a Birds team featuring its backup quarterback while missing a slew of starters wouldn't be a great sign.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker Reacts to Revenge Game vs. Seahawks, Patrick Mahomes Talks Chiefs RB's Return
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said he expects Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks to be "special" for Kenneth Walker III shortly after the running back downplayed his own focus on reuniting with his former teammates.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said he expects Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks to be "special" for Kenneth Walker III shortly after the running back downplayed his own focus on reuniting with his former teammates.

Walker will return to Lumen Field for the first time since his Super Bowl LX MVP run with the Seahawks this Sunday.

"I know it's going to be a special moment for him," Mahomes told reporters Wednesday. "You go back to the place where you built your career, where you won a Super Bowl. I know how special that is being here. Those fans are the people that were around him for all of that. Those are a still a lot of the guys that were his teammates that he grew up with, as well, as in the NFL."

Mahomes concluded, "At the end of the day, you've got to win a football game. He knows that we have his back."

Walker previously declined to add similar gravity to the situation when asked after the Chiefs' Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers last Sunday whether it would feel "different" to play against the Seahawks.

"We've got to go critique the mistakes that we made," Walker said about the Week 6 win. "And then, once we get to that point, we'll see."

Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Wednesday he felt Walker would take a "level-headed" approach to the matchup even if he receives special attention from the Seahawks defense.

"The one thing that, when you're on a team, everyone knows your strengths and weaknesses... I'm sure the boys there will try to get after him a little bit," Reid said . "He's a pretty level-headed guy... he's kind of got one speed. He's coming at you, and it doesn't really matter who he's playing, where he's playing."

The Chiefs agreed to a three-year, $43 million deal this offseason with Walker, who The Athletic's Michael-Shawn Dugar reported Wednesday did not receive an offer from the Seahawks ahead of hitting free agency.

Walker has since rewarded the Chiefs for making him one of the NFL's highest-paid running backs by racking up a league-high 665 rushing yards with six touchdowns through five games.

The Seahawks, which have so far this season deployed one of the NFL's top run defenses, will be tasked with limiting Walker for the first time since drafting him in 2022 when the Week 7 matchup kicks off Sunday night at 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Reacts to Being Named Giants QB1 Over Winston After Leading Comeback Bid vs. Saints
articles.summary: J.J. McCarthy reacted to being named the New York Giants' starting quarterback over Jameis Winston on Wednesday.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy reacted to being named the New York Giants' starting quarterback over Jameis Winston on Wednesday.

McCarthy told reporters that he was honored but "not surprised."

The Giants sent a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy during a Sept. 28 trade .

He initially sat behind Winston on New York's depth chart, but received an opportunity against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday.

While the Giants trailed 34-10 in the fourth quarter before McCarthy entered the contest, he helped them cut the deficit to 34-27. New York also had an opportunity to tie the game on its final drive, but failed to convert on fourth down in the Saints' red zone.

McCarthy finished 11-of-21 for 243 yards and one touchdown to go along with one interception in the fourth. He also rushed for 26 yards.

The 23-year-old will become the Giants' third starting quarterback this season, as Winston previously stepped in after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2.

McCarthy was initially selected by the Vikings with the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, but wasn't able to live up to his draft status.

He missed his rookie season due to a torn meniscus before completing just 57.6 percent of his passes for 1,632 yards and 11 touchdowns compared to 12 interceptions in 10 appearances during his 2025 campaign.

Kyler Murray eventually beat out McCarthy for the Vikings' starting quarterback role in training camp this year.

Now, McCarthy will get ready to face a Houston Texans defense that ranks No. 27 among all teams by allowing 246.0 passing yards per game this season.

Kickoff between New York and Houston is on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Sean McVay Updates Rams' WR Plans After Davante Adams Injury Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Wednesday that the team hasn't spoken internally about bringing in another wide receiver as wideout Davante Adams recovers from a ruptured left semitendinosus (hamstring muscle) suffered last Sunday vs. the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Wednesday that the team hasn't spoken internally about bringing in another wide receiver as wideout Davante Adams recovers from a ruptured left semitendinosus ( hamstring muscle ) suffered last Sunday vs. the Arizona Cardinals.

Adams, a six-time Pro Bowler and three-time First Team All-Pro, will undergo surgery and miss six-to-10 weeks .

Adams is in his second year with the Rams after signing a two-year deal in March 2025 . He made a strong impact in his first season, catching 60 passes for 789 yards and 14 receiving touchdowns, an NFL high.

The 13-year veteran continued his success in 2026, catching 30 passes for 480 yards and four touchdowns in six games. His season included an eight-catch, 195-yard, two-touchdown effort in a 28-6 win over the New York Giants and a seven-catch, 137-yard effort in a 30-26 loss against the Denver Broncos.

However, it's been a rough start for the 2-4 Rams, a preseason Super Bowl favorite that has suffered multiple injuries. Los Angeles has also played poorly in the back half of games, and now the Rams face an uphill battle.

Losing Adams is a tough blow, though he could return shortly after the Week 11 bye.

In the meantime, Rams wideout Puka Nacua will remain the team's top target. Konata Mumpfield is in line to be the team's WR2. The second-year pro has eight catches for 127 yards and a score. L.A. should also continue to use its tight ends, namely Tyler Higbee, who is fourth on the team in catches (24).

Los Angeles continues its season on Sunday at the Las Vegas Raiders.

articles.title: Former Patriots linebacker Brandon Spikes says he 'took a paycut' going from Florida to NFL

After a decorated college career which included two All-American selections and two national championships, Spikes was drafted late in the second round of the 2010 NFL Draft by the New England Patriots, where he spent five of his seven seasons in the league. "Those same home-cooked meals I got my whole life, I got those right there in Gainesville," he joked. If you are one of the few fans still believing kids weren't getting paid before the advent of NIL, I'm sorry to burst your bubble, but players like Spikes were living large long before it was "legal" to do so. articles.title: Former Chiefs, Falcons defensive end Allen Bailey dead at 37
articles.summary: Former Kansas City Chiefs and Atlanta Falcons defensive end Allen Bailey died at 37 years old. He was reportedly found dead in his Florida home.
articles.body: Former Kansas City Chiefs and Atlanta Falcons defensive end Allen Bailey died Tuesday at 37. Bailey's brother, Alford Bailey Jr., told TMZ that Bailey's wife found him dead at their Florida home on Tuesday. Bailey's family believes he died of natural causes, according to TMZ. No official cause of death has been released. "Allen Bailey was an excellent teammate, generous man, and kind soul. We're deeply saddened to hear of his passing, and our thoughts and prayers are with his family and friends," the Chiefs posted in a statement. Bailey spent the first eight seasons of his career with the Chiefs before signing a two-year, $10.5 million contract with the Falcons in 2019. In March 2020, the Falcons gave Bailey a one-year, $4.5 million contract extension, but released him in 2021 to save $4.5 million. He never played in the NFL again. In 10 seasons, Bailey played in 133 games (including 70 starts), recording 248 tackles and 22 sacks. Chiefs coach Andy Reid called him one of his favorite players. articles.title: Josh Jacobs says he's 'remorseful' as he returns to Packers following arrest, ongoing NFL investigation
articles.summary: Jacobs is eligible to play in Week 7 against the Lions.
articles.body:
Josh Jacobs spoke to reporters on Wednesday for the first time since he was removed from the commissioner's exempt list late last week.

The Green Bay Packers running back missed the first six weeks of the season while the NFL investigated Jacobs' offseason arrest for domestic abuse in May. Jacobs was placed on the list on Aug. 30.

"Excited to be back with the team, with the guys. I want to say thank you to the organization really for supporting me throughout this whole process and how everything played out. With that being said, I can't really get into a lot of things, like specifics of things, but obviously I'm remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation. Sometimes when you go through life situations occur, and a 4-second, 3-second decision can alter your life honestly. With that being said, still a human being, man, still trying to learn, still trying to grow from the whole process. Actually learned a lot throughout this whole process, legally and just personally.

With that being said, I can't really get into a lot of things, like specifics of things, but obviously I'm remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation.

Sometimes when you go through life situations occur, and a 4-second, 3-second decision can alter your life honestly. With that being said, still a human being, man, still trying to learn, still trying to grow from the whole process. Actually learned a lot throughout this whole process, legally and just personally.

Going forward just trying to be better. I know for some people this might be a stain on me and my character. I feel like I don't have to really speak on my character. A lotta people that know me in this locker room, or that's been around me, I'll let them do that. For me, man, I'm just trying to come back in here, play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward."

Going forward just trying to be better. I know for some people this might be a stain on me and my character. I feel like I don't have to really speak on my character. A lotta people that know me in this locker room, or that's been around me, I'll let them do that.

For me, man, I'm just trying to come back in here, play ball, learn from this mistake and move forward."

The league's investigation into Jacobs is ongoing, and the NFL said his removal from the list does not affect it.

Jacobs was arrested in northern Wisconsin on May 26 and charged with multiple counts of domestic abuse. The charges stemmed from an incident three days prior, when Jacobs allegedly grabbed a woman trying to leave his garage and threw her to the ground.

The running back was formally charged with two of those counts, battery and criminal damage to property, the week before he was placed on the commissioner's exempt list. He pleaded no contest to both charges last month.

Jacobs filed a civil suit last week calling for an injunction and protective order surrounding the evidence, including footage of the incident, that would restrict access to records in his case. The Brown County district attorney has reportedly said that surveillance footage outside Jacobs' garage corroborates the victim's account of the incident.

In a statement, Jacobs' attorneys, Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Schonfeld, said he was "excited to get back to work" after being removed from the list.

"Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions," the statement said, via The Ringer's Tom Pelissero . "Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world. Since there are ongoing legal matters, he will not have any further comment."

Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur also spoke to reporters Wednesday about Jacobs' return.

"I think a lot of times you get in a situation where you might not make the right decision. I think people learn from their mistakes. He's extremely remorseful. I do believe he is a good person. I've been around him quite a bit. I believe in second chances."

LaFleur said earlier in the week that Jacobs' status for the game is still to be determined.

"We feel like he's in a pretty good spot. He's been training, but he's missed the exposure to football. [His availability] is going to be determined throughout the course of the week, see where he's at, see how he's feeling, and then we'll make a decision."

The Packers play the Detroit Lions on Sunday, and Jacobs is eligible to play if LaFleur and Green Bay believe he is ready.

articles.title: Jameis Winston Reacts to Benching in New Video After J.J. McCarthy Named Giants QB1
articles.summary: The New York Giants are making a change at quarterback this Sunday and starting J.J. McCarthy over Jameis Winston at the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are making a change at quarterback this Sunday and starting J.J. McCarthy over Jameis Winston at the Houston Texans.

On Wednesday, reporters asked Winston about the move, and the signal-caller took the high road in his response.

Winston took over as QB1 after Dart suffered a season-ending left knee injury on Monday, Sept. 21 at the Los Angeles Rams. He started the team's next four games. For the season, Winston has completed 57.0 percent of his passes for 957 yards (6.1 yards per attempt), seven touchdowns and five interceptions.

Last Sunday, Winston and the Giants got off to a rough start and fell behind 34-10 in the fourth quarter. Winston threw for 152 yards and a score but also tossed a pair of interceptions and had just 3.2 adjusted yards per attempt. He was also sacked four times.

Head coach John Harbaugh elected to make a change and inserted McCarthy into the lineup. McCarthy's first drive ended with an interception, but he caught fire and nearly led the Giants on an incredible comeback before they fell short 34-27.

McCarthy threw for 243 yards and a touchdown (plus the pick) while adding 26 rushing yards on two carries.

In a weak NFC East where the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys are 2-4 and the Washington Commanders are 1-4-1, the 3-2-1 Giants have a legitimate chance to emerge as division winners.

Ultimately, Harbaugh feels McCarthy gives this team the best chance right now in a surge for a postseason spot, and he'll lead the team on Sunday in Houston.

articles.title: NFL Playoff Picture Week 7: All 4 NFC North teams are in the field for now
articles.summary: Here is the current playoff field entering Week 7, listed by divisional seed.
articles.body:
Entering Week 7, we're about only one-third of the way through the regular season. So what good is a playoff lookahead this early, especially one where last season's champs (Seahawks) and this season's favorites (Rams) are not included?

On the one hand, if we look at the Week 6 standings from the 2025 season , you'd notice that the Colts and Buccaneers were the top two seeds in each respective conference. Neither team ended up making the playoffs.

On the other hand, the fields were not that out of whack from what we eventually saw in the playoffs. Six of the seven AFC teams and five of the seven NFC teams that were in the playoff field after Week 6 eventually made the postseason.

So there are certainly some big-picture things we can take from the current playoff field. It gives some perspective on just how much ground preseason playoff favorites, such as the Rams and Texans, have to make up if they want in on the playoff party come January.

It also shows just how strong the NFC North is now, with all four teams currently projected to make the postseason. Since the playoff format expanded in 2020, no division has ever landed all four teams in a single playoff field.

Here is the current playoff field entering Week 7, listed by divisional seed:

The unbeaten Chiefs own the best point differential (plus-57) in the NFL, and three of their five victories have been quite comfortable. Kenneth Walker III (655 rushing yards, the most ever by a player in his first five games with a team) has been a godsend, Patrick Mahomes has looked mostly terrific coming off injury, and KC's defense is allowing the second-fewest points per game. But they haven't faced a battering ram of a schedule so far, and six of their next eight games are on the road, so we are going to find out just how real they are over the next two months.

Buffalo hits the bye week in great shape at 5-1, but there have been some close-shave victories (and a home loss to the Patriots) among them. Josh Allen has been mostly tremendous in leading the NFL's top-scoring offense, but he's also had to do most of the heavy lifting at times. The run defense has shown improvement from a year ago, but virtually every other aspect of the defense as a whole could use improvement. It will be interesting to see if general manager Brandon Beane can make any personnel improvements on that side of the ball prior to the trade deadline.

The Jaguars have backed up their 13-win season with a strong 4-2 mark to start this year, although losses to the Broncos and Texans both featured second-half breakdowns after holding fourth-quarter leads. On the whole, Jacksonville has performed like a playoff-caliber team, with Trevor Lawrence playing well and Travis Hunter starting to impact games in more ways. The remaining schedule looks favorable on the surface, with the lowest opponent win percentage (.409), and yet seven of the final 11 games are away from home.

This season's early darlings, who incredibly are likely a dropped punt snap away from being 5-1, are 2-0 in the division with wins over the Steelers and Ravens. Deshaun Watson has been functional on the whole but especially good in second halves. This remains a low-scoring offense (17.7 ppg) with pass-protection issues and a lack of run-game punch. Cleveland's defense has been on the rise, keeping four of the past five opponents to 19 points or fewer, but the Browns will have to find ways to make life easier on themselves with all four AFC North teams currently over .500.

The season started on a sour note, as Drake Maye struggled and the defense could do only so much to help out. The arrow has pointed up in recent weeks as Maye has gotten back on track and A.J. Brown has returned to the lineup, although his first full game in Week 6 was forgettable. Keeping pace with the Bills will be tough with four of the next five games away from home and some high-profile matchups left, including current unbeatens Minnesota and Kansas City in Weeks 14 and 15.

There's a lot to figure out on offense, where play-calling duties have already shifted from Davis Webb back to Sean Payton — and the early results have been even worse than before. On the season, the Broncos average a league-worst 4.6 yards per play. Denver's two losses, both on the road, have each been by double digits. Its four victories have all been one-score affairs. Defensively, the Broncos have lived and died on sacks and turnovers but have been leaky against the run, with poor tackling. Payton has a tough, competitive team, but until Bo Nix and the offense get going, they're also an incomplete one.

Aaron Rodgers has 12 TD passes and is on pace for his best passing totals since his MVP campaign in 2021, but he's averaging a turnover per game. The Steelers needed overtime to beat the Buccaneers and lost their other two road outings. With the Ravens and Bengals right on their heels, the Steelers will need to continue forcing turnovers on defense and cut back on them on offense. Their margin for error feels a little slim, even with the 4-2 start to the season.

Even after Monday's scare against the Commanders, it's been hard to argue with much of what we've seen from the Niners this season. They're 6-0, including 3-0 in the division with head-to-head road victories over the Rams and Seahawks, the presumed NFC West faves entering the season. Brock Purdy is playing at an MVP level, and the defense has been improved, even if there's a need for more big plays. One thing to watch: Mike Evans' health. The 49ers are a different team with and without him on the field. Losing him, on top of all their other injuries, would be a major blow to their No. 1 seed chances.

They're 5-0 but ripe for questions given the state of the offense right now. Kyler Murray is back under center after missing parts of two games, and they've had the bye week to make adjustments, but they'll need to find ways to be more explosive. Brian Flores' defense is absolutely smothering opponents, averaging two forced turnovers per game and giving up 513 pass yards the past four games combined, but can this unit carry the team all season? There's also the matter of the remaining strength of schedule, which is a whopping .572, with several tough opponents ahead.

Bryce Young is off to a terrific start, and the Panthers' offense is starting to resemble a pretty interesting unit. Chuba Hubbard has anchored the run game, and the offensive line hasn't been the concern area some thought it might be. After allowing 59 points in the opener, the Panthers have settled down a bit, giving up only 64 in the four games since. There's still room for improvement on that side, but the arrow is pointing up. With more home games (seven) than road games (five) remaining, and amid a weaker NFC South, there's a pretty good runway for the Panthers to make the postseason two straight years.

The move to start J.J. McCarthy feels like an inflection point on the season. The Giants currently lead the morass that is the NFC East, but they're going to need better QB play consistently from here on out to hang onto the division lead. All three wins have come at home, and they have yet to win on the road, which is where the next two games are, with the bye in between. John Harbaugh has helped make the team more competitive, but the defense needs to make more big plays to keep them ahead of a weakened division.

The Packers' season looked wayward after the 1-2 start, but three straight victories have changed the trajectory, especially with Jordan Love starting to take command of the offense. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson are fueling the vertical passing game again, even if there has been some meat left on the bone. Don't overlook the contributions of the defense, either. In the past three games, they've forced nine turnovers and allowed only 34 points. This unit could ascend even higher once Micah Parsons returns, but it might be a few more weeks' wait.

It has been a tale of three mini-seasons in one: before Caleb Williams' injury, the three games he missed, and after his return. With Williams, the Bears feel like a frightening team capable of taking down almost anyone; without him, it's hard to imagine the Bears threatening quality opponents. Defensively, it appears they need to force turnovers to be effective, allowing the most yards per play in the NFL. The schedule also figures to be a grind, with several tough opponents remaining, and they'll have to do something about their 0-2 mark in the division.

It has been an uneven start thus far for the Lions, but they're in the playoff field as of now, thanks to an offense that puts up the second-most points per game at 32.8. The problem, of course, is a defense that gives up nearly 30 points and more than 400 yards per game. They have shown a better pass rush, and the secondary could welcome Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph back at some point, but vast improvement is needed. They're coming off a bye with two huge games at home upcoming against the Packers and Vikings. Win those and the Lions can really help their chances of reclaiming the NFC North.

articles.title: Sam Franklin Jr becomes second Bills player suspended over alleged spitting, appeals NFL ban
articles.summary: Sam Franklin denied the spitting allegation on Instagram and posted video showing Delmar Glaze appearing to strike him during the Raiders game.
articles.body: Buffalo Bills safety Sam Franklin Jr. maintains he did not spit on a Raiders player during last week’s game in Las Vegas. He is appealing the NFL’s one-game, unpaid suspension, sources told ESPN and The Associated Press on Wednesday. The appeals process is not public. However, under the collective bargaining agreement, appeals are heard by one of four people: former players Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson and James Thrash, or former coach Ron Rivera. The NFL and NFLPA jointly appointed the panel. Franklin reportedly filed his appeal the same day the NFL announced its disciplinary action. According to the league, "Franklin will be suspended one game without pay because of an incident that occurred with 1:32 remaining" in Buffalo’s 33-30 win last week. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Franklin is now the second Bills player to be suspended by the league for a spitting-related incident stemming from Week 6. Fellow Buffalo defensive back, C.J. Gardner-Johnson also received a one-game suspension after the league determined spitting in the direction of Raiders players. Gardner-Johnson, who won a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles, appeared to spit in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. In both cases, the suspensions were issued after the players were found to have violated NFL Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which outlines discipline for any act that is "contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship." Other details surrounding Franklin’s discipline were not immediately revealed by the league. RAMS TACKLE ALARIC JACKSON WINS APPEAL, WILL MISS JUST ONE GAME FOR PUNCHING BILLS' BRADLEY CHUBB Franklin denied the allegation in a message posted on his Instagram account, saying he’s "Not a dirty play what so ever! Will always defend myself though. Still won't spit on anyone." His social media post included a slow-motion replay showing Las Vegas offensive lineman Delmar Glaze appearing to strike Franklin in a sensitive area below the waist during the Raiders’ successful extra-point attempt in what was ultimately a Bills victory. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The clip ends before the play is over and does not show any of Franklin’s retaliation. It is not clear whether Franklin spit at anyone. RAMS OFFENSIVE LINEMAN PUNCHES BILLS LINEBACKER AFTER THRILLING GAME: 'TEMPERS GOT FLARED' The timing of the appeals hearing was not immediately available. The Bills have a bye weekend and Franklin’s suspension was set to begin Monday and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. As for Gardner-Johnson, the safety was ejected for his action during the second quarter, which was captured by TV cameras and replayed during the broadcast. Following the game, Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates. He also told reporters, "I’ll take my consequences," while adding that he has to be better at controlling his emotions. Franklin, meanwhile, was not initially penalized following the play. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD A video posted on social media by an NFL Network reporter shows a scuffle occurring following the successful PAT, with Glaze blocking Bills linebacker Michael Hoecht while at the same time pulling Franklin’s undershirt. Franklin responded by shoving Glaze from the side. Glaze then turned to Franklin and appeared to shove the Bills player’s helmet. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Giants' Malik Nabers named FedEx Air & Ground NFL Player of the Week
articles.summary: New York Giants WR Malik Nabers has been named the FedEx Air & Ground NFL Player of the Week for Week 6.
articles.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers has been named the FedEx Air & Ground NFL Player of the Week for Week 6.

The fan-voted honor recognizes his performance in the Giants' 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints at MetLife Stadium on Sunday.

Nabers caught 12 of 15 targets for 165 yards, with a long of 46 yards. He led New York in receptions, targets, and receiving yards while averaging 13.8 yards per catch. It was his third consecutive game with at least 100 receiving yards.

Over that three-game stretch, the third-year wideout has totaled 29 catches for 398 yards and two touchdowns on 42 targets.

The output came with shifting quarterback play. Jameis Winston started but was benched in the fourth quarter after two interceptions in favor of J.J. McCarthy. Nabers stayed productive throughout, with a large share of his yardage arriving after the change.

The Giants generated 461 total net yards in the defeat.

Through six games, Nabers has 41 receptions for 494 yards and two scores. His target volume and reliability have made him the centerpiece of the Giants' passing attack as the team sits at 3-2-1.

The Giants next host the Houston Texans on Sunday.

articles.title: NFL RB Rankings Week 7: Kenneth Walker III Leads Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson in PFN’s Top 5
articles.summary: Kenneth Walker III has not merely solved the Kansas City Chiefs’ need at running back. Through the first six weeks of the 2026 season, he has played at a lev...
articles.body:
Kenneth Walker III has not merely solved the Kansas City Chiefs' need at running back. Through the first six weeks of the 2026 season, he has played at a level that stacks up with some of the best running back seasons in PFN's database.

Walker owns a 97.3 PFN Running Back Impact grade, comfortably ahead of Jahmyr Gibbs at No. 2. Chuba Hubbard, James Cook, and Bijan Robinson round out a top five featuring a mix of dominant rushing efficiency, receiving value, and enormous overall production.

PFN analyst Max Chadwick broke down the five highest-graded running backs entering Week 7. Running Back Impact blends rushing and receiving value over replacement with yards from scrimmage, touchdowns, and rushing yards over expectation to measure a player's total impact.

Bijan Robinson has produced more yards from scrimmage than any running back in football despite not leading the league in touches.

Robinson has 785 scrimmage yards on 138 touches. His 641 rushing yards rank second in the NFL, while he has added 144 receiving yards and five total touchdowns.

That production becomes even more impressive when considering his efficiency. Robinson has generated 8.9 rushing EPA this season, the second-best mark among qualified running backs, and he has gained 170 rushing yards over expectation.

Chadwick highlighted the relationship between Robinson's volume and production. He ranks fourth in total touches but first in scrimmage yards, meaning Atlanta has received more yardage from him than any other team has gotten from its running back despite several players handling the football more often.

That is the type of efficiency the Falcons envisioned when they used a first-round pick on Robinson. He has developed into one of the league's most complete backs, capable of creating explosive runs, producing after contact, and contributing as a receiver without needing an overwhelming workload to pile up yardage.

Robinson has already established himself as an elite NFL running back. His 2026 start has only reinforced that status.

James Cook has become an increasingly important part of a Buffalo offense that cannot consistently rely on its defense to control games.

Cook has 716 yards from scrimmage through six games, fifth-most among NFL running backs. He has rushed for 627 yards and six touchdowns while adding another 89 yards through the air.

The efficiency metrics are also among the league's best. Cook has generated 5.9 rushing EPA and 106 rushing yards over expectation, putting him near the top of the position in both categories.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Chadwick also pointed to how far Cook has come since entering the league. Much of the discussion around him early in his career centered on whether he could become anything close to the type of NFL running back his older brother, Dalvin Cook, had been.

James Cook has now developed into a star in his own right.

His ability to create efficient rushing production gives Buffalo something beyond asking Josh Allen to carry the offense on virtually every important down. Allen remains the engine of the Bills, but Cook's emergence has made the offense far less one-dimensional.

The raw production, efficiency, and touchdown output have combined to give Cook an 85.1 grade and the No. 4 spot in PFN's rankings.

Chuba Hubbard doesn't have the same volume as the other backs near the top of the rankings, but what he has done with his opportunities has been exceptional.

Hubbard has produced 511 yards from scrimmage and six touchdowns on 103 touches. His 426 rushing yards rank ninth among qualified running backs despite his lighter workload, and he has added 85 receiving yards.

His PFN efficiency metrics explain why his grade is considerably higher than the counting stats might suggest. Hubbard has generated 6.8 rushing EPA, fourth-best at the position, and his 9.6 receiving EPA leads all running backs.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

That receiving number is particularly important. Hubbard isn't simply adding empty catches to his rushing production. His work as a receiver has consistently created positive value for Carolina's offense.

Chadwick's main takeaway was that the Panthers should be finding even more ways to involve him. Hubbard ranks only 14th among running backs in yards from scrimmage, largely because he hasn't received the same touch volume as the players around him in PFN's top five.

His 90.3 grade suggests the quality of those touches has been elite.

Hubbard has already turned himself into one of the league's most productive backs on a per-opportunity basis. Increasing his workload could allow the traditional box-score numbers to begin matching the underlying performance.

Jahmyr Gibbs has been one of the most productive fantasy players in football, but the numbers driving that production extend well beyond fantasy scoring.

Gibbs has 738 yards from scrimmage and nine touchdowns through five games. His touchdown total leads all NFL running backs, while his scrimmage-yard total trails only Robinson and Walker.

He has rushed for 504 yards on 105 attempts and added 234 receiving yards on 27 catches. Only a handful of backs can match his ability to create high-end production in both phases of the offense.

PFN's data reflects that balance. Gibbs has generated 4.5 rushing EPA and 6.5 receiving EPA, giving Detroit positive value whether it uses him as a conventional runner or creates opportunities for him in space.

His Week 5 performance against the Arizona Cardinals showed the entire package. Gibbs rushed 25 times for 151 yards and two touchdowns while catching five passes for another 56 yards, finishing with 207 yards from scrimmage.

Those two touchdowns also put him in NFL history. Gibbs moved past Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns ever scored by a player before his 25th birthday. Gibbs now has 58 career touchdowns and does not turn 25 until March.

Chadwick described Gibbs as the latest potentially legendary running back in Detroit after Sanders. That comparison carries enormous weight, but Gibbs' early-career touchdown production has already placed his name next to one of the greatest backs the sport has seen.

His 93.6 PFN grade is elite. It still isn't enough to catch the player ranked first.

1) Kenneth Walker III, Kansas City Chiefs

Kenneth Walker III has been in a tier of his own through his first five games with Kansas City.

The Chiefs signed Walker after his four seasons with the Seattle Seahawks, looking for a runner capable of taking some of the offensive burden away from Patrick Mahomes. The move has worked about as well as Kansas City could have hoped.

Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards on 106 carries, an average of 6.3 yards per attempt. He has another 95 receiving yards, giving him 760 yards from scrimmage and eight total touchdowns.

His efficiency metrics are even more extreme.

Walker has generated 12.6 rushing EPA, easily the best mark among running backs. He has also rushed for 277 yards over expectation. No other back is within 100 yards of that figure.

That means Walker hasn't simply benefited from Kansas City's offense or favorable blocking. He has consistently created significantly more yardage than the circumstances of his carries would normally produce.

His game logs reinforce the point. Walker rushed for 173 yards against Denver in Week 1, 117 against Indianapolis in Week 2, and 177 against Las Vegas in Week 4. After Kansas City's bye, he returned with another 128 yards and two touchdowns against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Walker has topped 100 rushing yards in four of his five games and already has seven runs of at least 20 yards.

The historical context may be even more impressive. When Chadwick compared Walker's 97.3 grade with PFN's historical database, it ranked seventh among running back seasons since the turn of the century. The six seasons ahead of him all finished with more than 2,000 yards from scrimmage.

That doesn't mean Walker is guaranteed to maintain this pace. PFN grades evolve as the sample grows, and there is plenty of football left. It does illustrate the level at which he has played through five games.

Kansas City wanted someone who could reduce how often Mahomes had to carry the entire offense. Instead, the Chiefs may have found the most effective running back in football.

articles.title: Jerry Jones vouches for Troy Aikman amid ESPN contract rumors
articles.summary: Once you are the quarterback of the Dallas Cowboys, your business becomes Jerry Jones’ business, and that extends to your post-playing media career. Just ask...
articles.body:
Once you are the quarterback of the Dallas Cowboys, your business becomes Jerry Jones' business, and that extends to your post-playing media career. Just ask Tony Romo and, now, Troy Aikman.

To catch everyone up to speed, Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports reported last week that "tension" has been brewing between Aikman and Buck, the voices of ESPN's Monday Night Football since 2022. Buck signed a six-year contract extension last month, while ESPN remains uncommitted to Aikman beyond this NFL season.

Aikman sounded like a man expecting to hit free agency, both on KTCK The Ticket and in an exchange with Jimmy Traina . Jerry Jones is keeping tabs on the unfolding saga and commented while leaving a two-day meeting amongst NFL owners in New York City.

"I sure am," Jones said, per Mark Maske of Front Office Sports . "I think the world of Troy. And I'm always very interested and so proud of what he's become, the person as well as the career he's having. And I'm proud of that, and it feels good to have been with him early as a player. So, yes, I pay a lot of attention to him."

Maske also relayed that NFL chief media officer Hans Schroeder has " no concern " about Aikman and Buck's dynamic on MNF .

In terms of Aikman's viability as an NFL front-office executive, Jones added, "Troy is very capable. And he's so really, relatively speaking, he's in his youth [in his] career. And he's very capable of doing [any] number of things, certainly having to do with football. I don't know of any area, short of getting back out there on the field […] that he's not qualified and competent to go into."

Given all the headlines about Aikman's status at ESPN, it flew relatively under the radar that Aikman is also reportedly in flux in his consultant role with the Miami Dolphins.

Jones also vouched for Romo , and it had zero impact on CBS's decision to part ways with Romo in favor of J.J. Watt, so keep that in mind when weighing Jones' comments about Aikman. Ultimately, ESPN will have to decide whether to retain Aikman or shake up the NFL's premier booth. It'll take a whole lot more than Jones' two cents to keep Aikman and Buck together.

articles.title: NFL WR Rankings 2026: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Is in a Tier of His Own Heading Into Week 7
articles.summary: No position in PFN’s NFL Impact rankings has a bigger gap between first and second place than wide receiver. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has followed his 2025 Offensi...
articles.body:
No position in PFN's NFL Impact rankings has a bigger gap between first and second place than wide receiver.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba has followed his 2025 Offensive Player of the Year campaign with an even more dominant start to 2026. His 98.7 PFN Wide Receiver Impact grade is 10.2 points higher than CeeDee Lamb's mark at No. 2, while Chris Olave, Christian Watson, and Drake London complete the top five entering Week 7.

PFN analyst Max Chadwick broke down the league's five highest-graded receivers, using PFN's Impact data to look beyond raw catches and receiving yards. Target share, receiving EPA, EPA per target, yards after the catch, separation, and other efficiency metrics help show how much value each receiver is creating with his opportunities.

Drake London has yet to catch a touchdown this season. That hasn't prevented him from ranking among the most productive receivers in football.

London has caught 31 passes for 550 yards through six games, putting him fourth in the NFL in receiving yardage. He has done that on 47 targets, giving him considerably fewer opportunities than several of the league's other receiving leaders.

That combination of production and opportunity stood out to Chadwick. London owns a 25.3% target share, but he has generated 28.3 receiving EPA and 0.60 EPA per target. He isn't accumulating yardage simply because Atlanta is forcing him the ball on every possession.

His work after the catch has been even more impressive. London is averaging 8.2 yards after the catch per reception, the best figure among any receiver in PFN's top five. His YAC+ figure of 70.1 means he has gained roughly 70 more yards after the catch than expected based on the situations in which he caught the football.

That is unusual production for a 6-foot-4, 213-pound receiver who is often associated more with winning contested catches and using his size than creating after the ball arrives.

London has also remained a strong separator, another reason his production has been sustainable despite the lack of touchdowns. If Atlanta's passing game continues putting him in these positions, the scoring opportunities should eventually follow the yardage.

Chadwick's ranking reflects what London has already done rather than what his touchdown total says. He has been one of the NFL's most efficient and productive receivers even without finding the end zone.

Christian Watson has always possessed the physical tools to become a legitimate No. 1 receiver. In 2026, the production has finally caught up to the potential.

Watson has 29 receptions for 538 yards and six touchdowns through six games. His 18.6 yards per reception are the highest among PFN's top five receivers, and only Smith-Njigba has caught more touchdowns.

The transformation becomes even clearer when looking at Watson's career grades. Before this season, he had never finished higher than 29th among wide receivers in PFN Impact. He is fourth now.

"He's playing like a bona fide No. 1 right now," Chadwick said.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

Watson isn't doing it through overwhelming volume, either. His 20.0% target share is easily the lowest among the five receivers on this list. He has drawn only 48 targets, yet he has produced 538 yards and six scores.

Watson has generated 24.2 receiving EPA and 0.50 EPA per target while averaging 5.7 yards after the catch. His YAC+ figure sits at 64.5, showing that his athleticism is producing value both downfield and once the ball is in his hands.

The explosive plays have been particularly important. Watson already has 10 receptions of at least 20 yards and three of 40 or more, with a long reception of 81 yards.

There was never much question about whether Watson had the speed and size to threaten NFL defenses vertically. The issue throughout the early part of his career was turning those traits into consistent high-level production. Chadwick believes that has finally happened.

The biggest positive for Chris Olave this season may simply be that he has been able to stay on the field and remind everyone how productive he can be when healthy.

Olave has caught 43 passes for 580 yards and two touchdowns, giving him the second-most receiving yards in the NFL behind Smith-Njigba. His 61 targets account for a 24.5% share of the New Orleans passing game.

His value goes well beyond the counting numbers. Olave has generated 39.1 receiving EPA, second only to Smith-Njigba among PFN's top five receivers. He is also producing 0.64 EPA every time he is targeted.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Chadwick has never viewed talent as the concern with Olave. Availability has been the larger issue throughout his career. When healthy, Olave's route running and ability to separate have consistently allowed him to create opportunities at every level of the field.

PFN's separation metric has him at 2.8 this season, while he has produced eight receptions of at least 20 yards and three of 40 or more.

The one area where there is obvious room for growth is touchdown production. Two touchdowns on 580 receiving yards is a modest scoring total, especially given how involved Olave is in the offense.

Still, Chadwick's ranking is based on what Olave is doing on individual opportunities rather than whether those opportunities happen to end in the end zone. His ability to consistently create positive value has him back among the NFL's highest-graded wide receivers.

Unlike several players in this top five, CeeDee Lamb's placement near the top of the rankings doesn't qualify as a breakout.

This is where he has lived for much of his career.

Lamb has 48 receptions for 577 yards and four touchdowns through six games. His 48 catches trail only Smith-Njigba among the league leaders, while his 577 receiving yards rank third.

Dallas continues to build a substantial portion of its passing game around him. Lamb has been targeted 71 times, the most of any receiver in PFN's current rankings, and owns a 27.7% target share despite George Pickens giving the Cowboys another dangerous receiving option.

Lamb has produced 24.5 receiving EPA with 0.35 EPA per target. His 3.7 yards after the catch per reception aren't as eye-catching as London's or Watson's figures, but he has still generated 10 yards above expectation after the catch.

The broader résumé is what separates Lamb from most NFL receivers. He ranked second in PFN's receiver grades in 2023 and fifth in 2022. After a couple of seasons outside the very top group, he has returned to No. 2 in 2026.

Chadwick described Lamb as everything a team wants from a true No. 1 receiver. He can win as a route runner, create after the catch, handle enormous target volume, and remain productive even when defenses know exactly where Dallas wants to send the football.

That profile would ordinarily make a strong case for the No. 1 spot. This season, however, the gap between Lamb and the receiver ahead of him is enormous.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba isn't merely No. 1 in PFN's wide receiver rankings. Through six weeks, he is operating in a completely different statistical tier.

Smith-Njigba leads the NFL with 717 receiving yards, 49 receptions, and seven touchdown catches. He has done it on 66 targets, five fewer than Lamb, while commanding a league-high 30.7% target share.

His 46.1 receiving EPA is also the best mark at the position. Smith-Njigba is creating 0.70 EPA per target while adding 4.3 yards after the catch on the average reception.

The yardage gap is already substantial. Smith-Njigba has 137 more receiving yards than Olave, who ranks second in the league, despite the season being only six games old.

That production has created a 98.7 PFN Impact grade. Lamb sits at 88.5 in second place, meaning Smith-Njigba has opened a 10.2-point advantage over every other receiver in football.

Chadwick believes the current pace belongs in a historical conversation.

Smith-Njigba already authored one of the best seasons of his generation in 2025. He caught 119 passes for an NFL-leading 1,793 yards and 10 touchdowns, earning AP Offensive Player of the Year honors while helping Seattle win the Super Bowl.

When Chadwick compared Smith-Njigba's current grade with PFN's historical database, the names around him were players producing iconic seasons. Cooper Kupp earned a perfect 100 grade during his 2021 Triple Crown season, when he finished with 1,947 receiving yards and 16 touchdowns. Randy Moss' 2007 season included an NFL-record 23 touchdown receptions.

Smith-Njigba is playing in that type of statistical neighborhood through six weeks.

The development becomes even more remarkable when considering where his career stood only a few years ago. Smith-Njigba totaled 628 receiving yards as a rookie in 2023. He improved to 1,130 in 2024 before exploding for 1,793 last season. Now he is on pace to challenge that career year almost immediately.

At this point, Chadwick doesn't need to make a complicated argument for why Smith-Njigba ranks first. He leads the position in catches, receiving yards, touchdowns, target share, receiving EPA, and overall PFN grade.

There are several elite receivers playing well in 2026. Through six weeks, none of them has been particularly close to Smith-Njigba.

articles.title: Josh Jacobs apologizes to teammates as he gets ready to play again amid ongoing NFL investigation
articles.summary: (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs apologized to teammates as he returned to practice Wednesday and talked to reporters for the first time sin...
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs apologized to teammates as he returned to practice Wednesday and talked to reporters for the first time since pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground.

"Obviously, man, I'm remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation," Jacobs said. "Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life, honestly."

Jacobs was removed this week from the commissioner's exempt list , which had prevented him from playing or practicing. The NFL had placed Jacobs on that list Aug. 30, shortly after charges were filed against him. He pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property.

The NFL is still investigating Jacobs over the incident, so the league still could hand out more discipline to the three-time Pro Bowl running back. But for now, Jacobs is eligible to play again for the Packers after missing the first six games of the season.

"I thought I'd be playing sooner," Jacobs said. "But, you know, the optics of everything, I understand the other side. For me, like I said, I'm just grateful to be able to play. It was one of them things where I didn't want to sit the whole year and then figure it out. I'm just grateful to be back on the team and to be back playing."

Jacobs doesn't discuss details of his arrest

Jacobs was arrested May 26, three days after police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground.

Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head.

The criminal complaint against him noted that a surveillance video from the camera system in their garage corroborated the woman's statement. Both Jacobs and the victim have gone to court attempting to have that video and other evidence sealed permanently.

Jacobs declined to discuss the specifics of his case but said he hopes to use the situation as an opportunity to grow into a better person.

"Obviously you never want to be in this situation, but just me being honest, for my life, it was probably one of the best things to ever happen to me," Jacobs said. "I say that because it gave me a chance to sit down and reevaluate what's important and what I want my life to look like, and what do I want people to know me for. When they think of me, what are they going to say?"

Jacobs didn't fear possibility he might not play again

Jacobs was asked Wednesday if he'd feared the possibility he might never play again after his arrest.

"I wasn't overly concerned about that because in my heart, I know what happened and what didn't happen," Jacobs said. "And I'll just trust the legal process. So for me, I wasn't ever overly concerned of not playing again. It was just a matter of when."

Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love said Jacobs had spoken to the team and that the Packers are "happy to have Josh back, for sure." Green Bay's offense ranks last in the NFL in yards rushing per game (59.8) and yards per carry (2.9).

Coach Matt LaFleur hasn't indicated what kind of workload Jacobs might get Sunday at Detroit, or even whether he would play at all. Jacobs was unable to practice or play while on the commissioner's exempt list, but he was able to attend meetings and lift weights and condition with the Packers' strength coaches.

"I think people learn from their mistakes and I think he's extremely remorseful and I do believe that he's a good person," LaFleur said. "I've been around him quite a bit and I just, I believe in second chances."

LaFleur's comment Wednesday was more measured than what he said Sept. 1, after the charges were filed but before Jacobs pleaded no contest to the two misdemeanors. LaFleur said then that "I believe him and I trust him" and added that "I'm going to do that until proven otherwise."

Jacobs was asked if he feels he needs to earn back the respect of teammates and what he would say to fans.

"I don't think I had to earn respect back from the guys because I'm the same person every day," Jacobs said. "Like I said, at the end of the day, we're human. We all make mistakes. It's just different for me because I'm in the public eye. But you know, like I said, I'll let other people speak to my character and who I am and who I consistently have been.

"When it comes to earning the respect of the fans, I mean, for me, it's more of a thing of not trying to put this organization in a position where it looks negative in any type of way. But at the end of the day, people are always going to have their opinion. People are going to believe what they believe, and it's not really my job to try to explain or discount certain things. All I can try to do is control what I can control and move on from there."

articles.title: Buccaneers Lineman Was Left Stunned After Steelers' Yahya Black Revealed True Weight
articles.summary: The Buccaneers tackle got a surprising answer from Pittsburgh's Yahya Black during a mic'd-up conversation.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers rookie Yahya Black gave Tampa Bay Buccaneers tackle Tristan Wirfs a surprising answer when the two linemen discussed their weight during a mic'd-up conversation captured by NFL Films.

Black, who is listed at 330 pounds on Pittsburgh's roster, told Wirfs he weighs 370 pounds.

"I knew it. You look huge," Wirfs responded before clarifying his remarks.

"No, I mean, you look great. You look like an absolute unit," Wirfs told the Steelers defensive lineman.

Wirfs also recalled Black's physical development during their time at Iowa, noting how much the defensive lineman had grown since his early college days.

The conversation took another humorous turn when Wirfs asked about the overalls Black wore for an Iowa game. Black revealed they were size 4XL, prompting Wirfs to tell him they looked good.

The NFL Films clip offers a candid look at the interactions between players, with Black's size standing out to one of the league's top offensive tackles.

articles.title: NFL fines Mike Vrabel, Aaron Glenn, Nick Sirianni $250,000 each for conduct toward officials
articles.summary: Fines are currently being held in abeyance, and could be repealed.
articles.body:
The NFL isn't messing around when it comes to behavior toward game officials. With an asterisk.

Albert Breer of SI.com reports that the NFL has fined Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, Jets coach Aaron Glenn, and Eagles coach Nick Sirianni $250,000 each for conduct toward game officials.

The discipline may be more performative that substantive. Breer explains that "the fines are in abeyance, meaning they'd be on hold, and could be repealed with good behavior."

It's not entirely clear where things stand, and what it would take to avoid the fines. Also, the amounts are borderline cartoonish. In 2012, former Patriots coach Bill Belichick was fined only $50,000 for confronting and grabbing the arm of a replacement official. Recently, 49ers owner Jed York was fined a mere $500,000 to go along with a six-game suspension after a prostitution-related arrest.

These fines seem over the top, especially since the specific behavior that prompted the fines has not been identified.

In Week 4, Vrabel was flagged for his comments to an official after a disputed call. "I told him it was a terrible — I'm not going to say effing — call," Vrabel said after the game. "I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach. It was nothing derogatory. You'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive ."

The league was more than a little sensitive. But it's not as if the $250,000 will be collected. All in all, it feels like an olive branch to the NFL Referees Association, after a pair of suspensions were imposed on officials for interactions with players in Week 5.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Bears 'Thursday Night Football' betting odds, picks and predictions: Best bets, player props
articles.summary: Our NFL handicapper break downs his favorite bets in the Patriots-Bears matchup on "Thursday Night Football."
articles.body:
Two of the hottest teams in the NFL square off Thursday when the suddenly resurgent Chicago Bears host the red-hot New England Patriots at Soldier Field.

Chicago (4-2) enters this clash fresh off a 31-23 road victory against the Atlanta Falcons. Quarterback Caleb Williams made a brilliant return from injury, completing 30 passes on 36 attempts for 305 yards and a touchdown.

On the other side, things couldn't be better for New England (4-2) and head coach Mike Vrabel. The Patriots have won three consecutive games, including last weekend's 26-19 triumph against the New York Jets.

The Bears opened as 1.5-point favorites and have taken a bunch of money since then, with the line now parked at -3 at most books across the landscape. The total has also jumped, moving from 47.5 to 50.5.

Let's take a look where we've found some betting value — and a live long shot — ahead of this intriguing showdown.

New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3, 50.5)

If there was a team inundated with injuries in Week 6, it was definitely New England.

The Patriots were beset with numerous injuries, specifically to their starting offensive linemen . Right guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and left guard Ben Brown (knee) have been ruled out. Right tackle Morgan Moses is dealing with a foot issue, but Vrabel said he has a chance of playing.

Obviously, that's a whole lot of key absences on the line protecting Drake Maye, who has been ridiculously good — and might be playing the best football of his young career — during this winning streak.

As for the Bears, you have to like their chances with Williams back under center. Chicago is a completely different team when he's leading the show, which was evident in last weekend's thrilling road win at Atlanta.

Another element working in the Bears' favor on the short week will be the emotional edge. This is the first game Chicago will be playing at Soldier Field since the passing of legendary coach/player Mike Ditka. Head coach Ben Johnson's team will hope to put together its finest performance against this same franchise Ditka and his 15-1 Bears squad defeated 46-10 in Super Bowl XX in New Orleans.

Statistically, these franchises can light it up on any given outing. New England averages just under 23 points per game, while Chicago is slightly better (25 PPG) in the category. The Bears have the edge for total yards per game (388.3 to 374.2), which could mean more fireworks.

Defensively, they're both solid. The Patriots rank 10th in total yards allowed (1,805), which is nine yards fewer than the 11th-ranked Bears. They're both in the top 10 in rushing yards conceded, while Chicago is tied for fifth with 17.0 total sacks.

The edge on these short-week games typically lies with the home team, but I think Vrabel will have New England ready to roll. The injuries to multiple offensive linemen are of major concern, but I think the Patriots' reserves will step up and fill the holes.

I think New England keeps this contest within a field goal — and potentially wins outright – on what is forecasted to be a picturesque night in the "Windy City."

Bet: Patriots +3.5 alternate spread (-140, FanDuel)

QB Drake Maye over 1.5 TD passes (-122, FanDuel)

Is there any quarterback in the NFL hotter than Maye right now? I think not.

Maye has been sensational of late, throwing for 878 yards and 10 touchdowns versus just one interception during the Patriots' three-game winning streak. He's also the first New England QB to have three consecutive games with at least three TD passes since Tom Brady, who achieved the feat in 2017.

Maye has cleared this number in three of his last five starts, so I don't see what's stopping him here. His numbers (18-of-35, 235 yards, three TDs) against the Jets would have been better had his receivers had made routine catches, including A.J. Brown and the three drops he had the win.

WR DeMario Douglas over 37.5 receiving yards (-114) | 40+ receiving yards (+100) | 50+ receiving yards (+168)

With Romeo Doubs now on the IR with a shoulder injury , Maye is going to have to find a complementary target to Brown in the New England offense.

We backed the speedy slot receiver to clear his yardage total in the Patriots' season-opening loss against the Seattle Seahawks. So, we have no problem going to the well with him one more time in a game where he should be featured even more with Doubs and fellow wideout Mack Hollins (calf) parked on the sideline.

Over the last two games, Douglas has been Maye's go-to guy. Douglas has 11 receptions on 13 targets for 151 yards and three touchdowns combined during that span. Douglas was second in targets to Brown in the victory against the Jets, finishing with a 59% snap share.

Jump on Douglas to clear his receiving yardage, then tack on a mini-ladder play for him to hit the alternate totals to 50 yards.

It goes without saying D'Andre Swift is the clear RB1 in the Chicago locker room.

He leads the Bears in carries (94), yards (398) and touchdowns (six) this season. However, something has stuck out over the last two Chicago games and that's his surprising inactivity getting the ball after halftime.

Swift has a grand total of five second-half carries over the last two games. Yes, you read that correctly. With Kyle Monangui out , I think you have to take a good, hard look at Johnson.

He put together his best effort of the season in the win against Atlanta, carrying the ball 13 times for 51 yards and a touchdown. He also had two catches for 34 yards.

With Swift getting shelved in the second half of late, I think this is a prime spot to target Johnson to score in back-to-back games.

This might look like a flyer on paper, but I think we're going to see more of Kiner than we think when New England lines up against the Chicago defense.

Vrabel obviously has confidence in the second-year running back out of Cincinnati. And his trust in Kiner was on full display last Sunday, when he had eight consecutive rushing attempts to close out the road win in New York.

Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' three-headed rushing attack with 13 carries for 57 yards, which came off the heels of his six-carry, 52-yard effort two weeks ago against Las Vegas.

He has yet to reach paydirt in his young career, but we're thinking this is the perfect night for his maiden touchdown. Getting this price makes backing Kiner that much more enticing in this showdown.
